30-MINUTE LAB
2 min: groups of three choose a task and assign roles.
Three 7-minute rounds: state the task, try it with minimal coaching, record evidence, propose one revision; rotate owner/tester/observer.
4 min: apply the same checklist to your own tool.
3 min: record one issue, one proposed revision, and one retest task.
Use concrete evidence: target identification, status feedback, hesitation, skipped objects, recovery, keyboard access. Do not grade a tool only on visual taste.
PACING
CORE SEQUENCE. Teach the visible task or question, then advance once students can explain the result.
Owner: state one artist task and its expected result, then observe without coaching. Tester: predict the next action, attempt the task and narrate uncertainty. Observer: record a visible event, its impact and one proposed change. Rotate roles. Apply the same checklist to your own tool after the review. If a peer tool is not runnable, label the review as a walkthrough and record what needs a live test. Capture one successful behavior and one revision to test.
